envelope.text: ADOPT-BOUNDED against rclrs: the duration-valued policies hold whole

why: ADOPTED 2026-10-27 (phase-515 R1): rclrs's `IntoPrimitiveOptions` / `PrimitiveOptions` in `nros_node::primitive_options` (re-exported from `nros` and its prelude), implemented for any borrowed string (`&T: Borrow<str>`, rclrs's own blanket) and for `PrimitiveOptions`. ENVELOPE (stated on the type): the duration-valued policies hold whole milliseconds, the unit `QoSProfile` records, so `deadline` / `lifespan` / `liveliness_lease` take a `core::time::Duration` where rclrs takes its `QoSDuration` enum, and the infinite case is `no_deadline` / `infinite_lifespan`; history and depth are two fields because `QoSProfile` keeps them apart. `Node::create_publisher` / `create_subscription` / `create_service` / `create_client` take it. Tests: `primitive_options::tests`, `create_sites_take_rclrs_primitive_options`. PRIOR ROW: rclrs's fluent per-create-site options: `node.create_publisher("topic".keep_last(10).reliable())` builds a `PrimitiveOptions` out of a `&str` and folds it into the entity's QoS. A user loses that spelling AT THE CREATE SITE. QoS and entity options are COMPILE-time here (RFC-0036/0045) -- an entity is declared with a `QoSProfile` const, not with an options value assembled per call -- so there is nothing for the builder to produce. The policy vocabulary itself is not lost: `QoSProfile` carries `keep_last`/`keep_all`/`reliable`/`best_effort`/`volatile`/`transient_local` under exactly these names, plus `deadline_ms`/`lifespan_ms`/`liveliness_kind`/`liveliness_lease_ms`/`avoid_ros_namespace_conventions` as fields. See `rust:QoSProfile`.
